full_text:
NSW Ambulance is urging people to prepare now with the Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) forecasting severe heatwave conditions for the South Coast.
NSW Ambulance Superintendent Bryce Picot, Senior Manager Emergency Management said people need to plan ahead and stay informed with this severe heatwave this weekend.
“Severe heatwave conditions are predicted to peak on Sunday and, with this being the first major heatwave of the season, it’s a good reminder that the real danger isn’t just one hot day, it’s the relentless heat over consecutive days,” Superintendent Bryce Picot said.

Locations likely to be impacted include Batemans Bay, Bega and Nowra.
A heatwave is when the daytime (maximum) and nighttime (minimum) temperatures are unusually hot over three days or more, which can pose serious risks to your health.
NSW Ambulance has issued an Advice warning for this severe heatwave. Stay up to date in case the situation changes.
Stay hydrated – make sure you drink plenty of water and carry a water bottle with you.
Keep cool – seek cool places, use air-conditioning or fans, draw your blinds, take cool showers and dress in light and loose clothing made of natural fabrics.

Avoid the heat – schedule activities in the coolest part of the day and avoid exercising in the heat.
Check in on vulnerable people – hot weather can affect everyone, but some people are at greater risk of heat-related health problems. This includes people aged 65 years and older, babies and young children, pregnant women, outdoor workers, socially isolated people, people experiencing homelessness and people with some medical conditions.
Never leave children or pets in a vehicle – leaving children or pets unattended in a car can be fatal. The temperature inside a parked car can double in minutes.
Store food and medications at a safe temperature – follow your doctor’s advice and store medicines in a cool place, most should be stored below 25 degrees Celsius.
“Signs of heat-related illness can include headache, dizziness, nausea and vomiting, fatigue and cramps,” Superintendent Picot said.

“People with these symptoms should move out of the sun and seek shade or use a fan or air conditioning, take a cool shower or bath if possible and take sips of water’” he said.
“If you, or someone you know, has signs or symptoms of heat-related illness, seek medical help. Call 1800MEDICARE on 1800 633 422 for free instant health advice anytime, anywhere.
“People who do not respond to these steps or who show symptoms suggesting a more severe illness, including a sudden rise in body temperature, who are no longer sweating, showing aggressive or strange behaviour or who are fitting, should seek urgent medical attention or call Triple Zero (000).”
For further information, updates and advice go to the NSW Ambulance website or follow NSW Ambulance on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and X.
For the latest weather forecasts and heatwave warnings go to the Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) website.
